in_scope: User authentication and role-based access control
Creation, modification, and deletion of test cases and suites
Manual and automated execution logging of test runs
Real-time dashboard showing pass/fail metrics and trends
RESTful API for CI/CD tool integrations
out_of_scope: In-browser containerized execution of selenium/playwright scripts
Integration with legacy mainframes without API access
assumptions: Users have access to modern web browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge)
Automated runs will push data via standard HTTPS API requests
Initial usage will not exceed 100 concurrent write operations per second
constraints: Must comply with standard enterprise data privacy standards (GDPR/CCPA)
Must be deployed in a secure VPC with restricted public database access
Maximum budget for cloud resources during initial MVP is $150/month

requirements.description: The system must allow users to create, read, update, and delete Test Cases.
The system must support organizing individual Test Cases into logical Test Suites.
The system must provide an API endpoint to ingest automated execution results.
All API endpoints for reporting execution metrics must respond in under 200 milliseconds.

user_roles.name: QA Engineer
user_roles.description: Creates and manages test cases, manually logs test executions, and analyzes results.

user_roles.name: QA Lead
user_roles.description: Manages test suites, configures integrations, and views high-level quality reports.

features.name: Test Case Registry
features.description: A centralized repository containing structured test cases complete with preconditions, steps, and expected outcomes.

features.name: Execution Run Engine
features.description: A module to group tests, execute them, and store statuses (PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, SKIPPED).

user_stories.description: As a QA Engineer, I want to write detailed test steps and expected outcomes, so that my team can reliably verify app behavior.
As a QA Lead, I want to trigger and ingest the results of a test run from our Jenkins CI/CD pipeline so that release builds are automatically gated.

architecture.reasoning: A monolithic architecture is chosen to maximize delivery velocity, minimize operational overhead, and allow simple transaction boundary management for core models during early phases.

components.name: Web UI Client
components.responsibility: Renders user dashboard, test case builder, and test run tracking panels.

components.name: API Service Gateway
components.responsibility: Handles routing, rate limiting, and authenticates JWT tokens from client or API integrations.

components.name: Core Application Service
components.responsibility: Handles CRUD operations for suites/cases and business logic around execution state transitions.

relationships: Web UI Client communicates with API Service Gateway via HTTPS JSON REST APIs.
API Service Gateway delegates request payload validation and processing to Core Application Service.
Core Application Service reads and writes directly to Database repository layers.
data_flow: User saves new Test Case -> Web UI sends POST request to Gateway -> Gateway verifies token -> Core Service inserts record -> DB confirms -> Client updates UI state.

frontend.reason: Provides structured, modular component hierarchy for fast responsive workflows.
Accelerates UI development with utility-first classes and clean visual patterns.

backend.reason: Offers lightweight, non-blocking asynchronous event handling ideal for API ingestion throughput.

database.reason: Strong ACID compliance guarantees relational consistency of test-to-run mappings and run state records.

infrastructure.reason: Ensures reproducible environmental setups for local development, staging, and production.
Enables serverless container executions eliminating underlying EC2 node maintenance tasks.

relationships: TestCases.id has a one-to-many relationship with TestExecutions.test_case_id (1:N)

phases.name: Phase 1: Foundation & Core CRUD
phases.description: Establish basic application skeleton, setup relational schema, and finalize fundamental UI elements for test management.
milestones: Database connection and baseline schema migration verified
Test Case creation UI and API routes fully completed

phases.name: Phase 2: Executions & CI Integrations
phases.description: Deliver execution tracking system alongside secure developer API keys enabling headless triggers.
milestones: Secure API Token emission module online
Successful execution import verified via Jenkins test script pipeline
